name: PCA9539PW
title: PCA9539 and PCA9539R: 16-bit I2C-bus/SMBus I/O expander with interrupt output and reset input
summary: A 24-pin CMOS port expander that hangs 16 general-purpose I/O lines, in two 8-bit ports, off an I2C-bus or SMBus at up to 400 kHz. Each line is set to input or output and its read polarity chosen through register pairs; an open-drain INT output goes LOW when an input differs from its last-read value, and an active-LOW RESET input recovers the device. On the PCA9539 RESET returns every register to its default; on the PCA9539R it clears only the bus state machine and leaves the ports as they were. Two address pins give four addresses; the supply runs from 2.3 V to 5.5 V (3.0 V to 5.5 V for the /Q900 parts), and PCA9539PW is the PCA9539 in TSSOP24.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A master controller on a 5 V supply drives SCL and SDA and receives INT, and it drives the expander's RESET; each of these four lines has a 10 kΩ pull-up to VDD. A0 and A1 are grounded, so the address byte is 1110 100X. IO0_0 sinks an LED through 2 kΩ from VDD, IO0_2 drives the RESET of a second sub-system, and IO0_3 drives the enable of a bus switch joining lines A and B; these three are outputs. IO0_1 reads the INT of a sub-system, IO0_4 the ALARM of another, and IO0_5 a push button that connects it to VDD through a resistor; each of the three has a 100 kΩ pull-up. IO0_6, IO0_7 and IO1_0 to IO1_7 are ten inputs reading a numeric keypad.

parts.note: in series with the push button

circuits.title: LED drive with a high-value resistor across the LED
circuits.description: An I/O sinks LED current from VDD through a series resistor. A 100 kΩ resistor from VDD straight to the I/O pin holds the pin up at VDD while the LED is off, instead of about 1.2 V below it, so the supply current does not rise.
notes: LEDn is any one of the 16 I/Os.

circuits.title: LED on a supply above the device supply
circuits.description: The expander runs from 3.3 V while the LED and its series resistor hang from 5 V. With the LED off its pin then sits no lower than VDD, since the LED supply is at least 1.2 V above the device supply, and no extra supply current flows.
notes: LEDn is any one of the 16 I/Os.

circuits.title: Test circuit for switching times
circuits.description: A pulse generator, terminated by RT to ground, drives the input of the device under test. The output is loaded by CL to ground and by RL to a switch that selects VDD, open or GND. CL counts the capacitance of jig and probe; RT matches the generator's output impedance Zo.

operation.text: The PCA9539 and the PCA9539R differ in what RESET does. Both match the PCA9555 except that the I/O lines have no internal pull-up resistor, which cuts supply current when lines are held LOW, that pin A2 is replaced by RESET, and that the address range differs.
The address byte starts with the fixed bits 11101, then A1 and A0 from the address pins, then R/W. Four devices can share a bus.

After the address in a write, the next byte is a command that points to one of eight registers (0 to 7). The registers work as four pairs, port 0 and port 1 of each: input, output, polarity inversion and configuration. Each further data byte in the same transfer goes to the other register of the pair, back and forth, so a write starting at Output port 1 puts the next byte in Output port 0. There is no limit on bytes per transfer, and each 8-bit register can still be written on its own.
Read-only. They show the logic level on each pin whether the pin is set as input or output. Writing to them does nothing.
They set the level driven on pins configured as outputs and have no effect on input pins. Reading them returns the flip-flop contents, not the pin level. Default is all 1s.
A 1 in a bit inverts that bit of the Input port register value the master reads; a 0 leaves it unchanged. Default is all 0s.
A 1 makes the pin an input with its output driver off (high impedance); a 0 makes it an output. Default is all 1s, so every line is an input after reset.

Each line has a high-side FET (Q1) to VDD and a low-side FET (Q2) to VSS. As an input both are off and the pin may be taken up to 5.5 V even above VDD. As an output one of the two conducts according to the output register bit, so a voltage forced onto an output pin meets a low-impedance path to VDD or VSS.

A built-in power-on reset keeps the device in reset until VDD rises past VPOR (1.7 V typ, 2.2 V max), then the registers and the SMBus state machine take their defaults. To reset it again by its supply, VDD has to fall below 0.2 V (for at least 5 µs) before being brought back.

Holding RESET LOW for at least tw(rst) resets the device. On the PCA9539 the registers and the I2C/SMBus state machine stay at default until RESET goes HIGH again. On the PCA9539R only the state machine is reset and the general-purpose registers keep their contents, so outputs hold their states while a bus stuck LOW is freed. RESET normally needs a pull-up to VDD. Resetting during bus traffic can cause glitches or false STOP conditions.

The master sends the address with R/W = 0, the command byte, then data; the device acknowledges each byte. An output change appears on the pins within tv(Q) (200 ns max) of the acknowledge clock edge of the data byte.

The master writes the address with R/W = 0 and the command byte, sends a repeated START, then the address with R/W = 1, and reads. The register takes in its data at the falling edge of each acknowledge clock. Further bytes alternate between the two registers of the pair, so after Input port 1 comes Input port 0. Any number of bytes may be read; the master does not acknowledge the last one. A STOP can end the transfer at any point.

INT, an open-drain output, goes LOW when an input-configured pin changes state, within tv(INT_N) (4 µs max). It is released when the pin returns to its earlier level or when the Input port register is read, within trst(INT_N) (4 µs max). Pins set as outputs never cause an interrupt. Ports are read separately, so reading port 1 does not clear an interrupt from port 0 and the reverse. Switching a pin from output to input can raise a false interrupt if its level differs from the Input port register contents.
SCL and SDA each need a pull-up resistor to a positive supply. Inputs carry a noise filter that suppresses spikes up to 50 ns (tSP), and the device starts without a glitch at power-up.

An LED driven from an I/O with its anode resistor to VDD leaves the pin about 1.2 V below VDD when the LED is off, and IDD rises as VI falls below VDD. Keeping the pin at or above VDD in the off state avoids that: a high-value resistor across the LED, or a device VDD at least 1.2 V below the LED supply.
Sinking: at most 25 mA on any I/O, 100 mA per 8-bit port and 200 mA for the device. Sourcing: at most 160 mA in total, 80 mA per 8-bit port.

The die ground connects to both the VSS pin and the exposed centre pad. The VSS pin must go to ground. The pad is soldered to a thermal land on the board, with thermal vias in that land, for heat, electrical and board-level performance.

All pins carry ESD protection for normal handling; handle to JESD625-A. Leaded packages with pitch below about 0.6 mm and leadless packages with lands under the body are not suited to wave soldering; leaded and leadless packages are reflow solderable. Peak reflow temperature by package thickness and volume follows J-STD-020D. Moisture sensitivity precautions on the packing apply.
